item.title: What does APEC's innovation priority look like on the ground in Shenzhen?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
What does innovation — one of APEC's three priorities this year — look like in practice? In Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen, it starts with an idea and finding the people who can help build it. Components, technical expertise and engineers come together here, giving makers from around the world a place to turn ideas into products.

item.title: Why ASEAN integration matters for the Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
As Asia-Pacific leaders prepare to gather in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov 18-19, they face a region that is more economically integrated than ever, yet increasingly vulnerable to fragmentation. While businesses depend on cross-border production networks, governments continue to impose trade restrictions and measures to protect domestic industries. This tension between economic interconnectedness and policy fragmentation has become a challenge for regional cooperation. China's APEC 2026 theme, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", emphasizes openness, innovation and cooperation — priorities that are both timely and crucial. The State of Southeast Asia 2026 Survey by the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute also reflects these priorities. When asked how the Association of Southeast Asian Nations should strengthen its resilience and relevance, 28.5 percent of the respondents favored increasing intra-regional trade and investment, while 20.7 percent supported diversifying supply chains to cushion economic tensions. In the face of rising protectionism and nationalism, the largest group of respondents favored accelerating regional integration. These findings suggest that ASEAN's preferred strategy against growing economic uncertainty is to strengthen internal economic ties while maintaining open partnerships beyond the region. Greater integration can create more opportunities within ASEAN, fortify supply chains, and make the region less vulnerable to external shocks. The survey also reveals a less discussed problem: 30.2 percent of the respondents identified limited domestic technocratic capacity to implement regional initiatives and 30.1 percent felt development disparities among member states were the leading impediments to intra-regional economic cooperation. Geopolitical pressures, while important, ranked behind these internal constraints. ASEAN has adopted numerous economic agreements and initiatives, but their effectiveness hinges on national-level implementation. Differences in regulatory capacity, infrastructure and digital readiness can hinder progress. The question is not whether ASEAN has sufficient instruments, but whether businesses, particularly micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, can practically benefit from these agreements. Singapore's 2027 ASEAN Chairmanship is an opportunity to advance this agenda. Singapore has prioritized deeper integration and stronger external partnerships. Achieving these goals would help ASEAN attract investment, expand partnerships beyond the region and strengthen its role in regional supply chains. To advance regional integration, ASEAN must address practical barriers to cross-border trade, including cumbersome customs procedures, inefficient logistics and differences in regulatory criteria. Greater technical cooperation and capability enhancement would also help less-developed member states implement regional commitments, enabling businesses, particularly MSMEs, to benefit more fully from regional integration. These efforts matter even more as companies adjust their supply chains to manage geopolitical and economic risks. China's manufacturing and technological strengths complement ASEAN's growing markets and production bases, alongside Singapore's role in logistics and financial services. The challenge is to maintain these economic ties while allowing businesses to diversify production and sourcing — without creating new trade barriers or dividing the region into competing economic blocs. Beyond trade in goods, digital integration is increasingly important. ASEAN's Digital Economy Framework Agreement, whose negotiations concluded in 2026, aims to facilitate digital trade and improve interoperability. If implemented effectively, it could reduce transaction costs and help smaller companies access regional markets through electronic documentation, digital payments and more compatible systems. The challenge will be to ensure that differences in national regulations and digital capabilities do not create new barriers. APEC plays a different but complementary role. While ASEAN advances integration through regional commitments, APEC brings together a broader group of economies for voluntary cooperation. It can promote trade facilitation, supply-chain connectivity, and compatible digital standards, even when members disagree on broader trade policy. The goal is not to establish identical rules, but to reduce unnecessary friction across markets. As the current APEC host and a major economic partner of ASEAN, China has a significant role to play. Economic cooperation will be judged by the sustainability and mutual benefits it delivers. The wider rules-based multilateral trading system, centered on the World Trade Organization, remains just as important. Smaller economies, in particular, rely on predictable rules rather than bargaining power alone. Regional arrangements should reinforce this system, not replace it. Although WTO reform remains difficult, Asia-Pacific economies share an interest in preserving common trade rules and preventing further fragmentation. Stronger ASEAN integration therefore matters beyond Southeast Asia. It can make regional production networks more resilient, sustain open partnerships and support wider Asia-Pacific cooperation. In a world of increasing protectionism, the priority should be to make existing frameworks deliver more effectively for businesses and communities, while preserving the common rules which support regional prosperity. The author is the former head of the External Relations Division of the ASEAN Secretariat and a senior fellow and coordinator at the ASEAN Studies Centre in the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute. The views don't necessarily reflect those of China Daily. item.title: In conversation with Cui Tiankai: US domestic noise should not derail China-US ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Before heading to Shenzhen to cover the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, we attended the US-China Political Dialogue 2026 held in Beijing. There, we spoke with Cui Tiankai, former Chinese ambassador to the US, about the key issues shaping China-US relations. Here are some of his key quotes from the interview: • The US ought to focus on fixing its own problems, rather than always looking elsewhere. • There are various noises and events inside the US. Some have absolutely nothing to do with China and shouldn't derail China-US ties. • The Pacific is vast enough for China and the US to grow together, and for the whole Asia-Pacific to thrive side by side. If the US joins us [China] and regional nations in this endeavor, we can achieve so much.

item.title: Gather in Shenzhen, witness the wonders
item.description:

APEC returns to China for the third time — landing in Shenzhen. From Shanghai to Beijing to Shenzhen, the themes build on one another. Check out with international reporters to see their expectations from this APEC.

item.title: Xi calls for jointly building Asia-Pacific community to prosper together
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping pledged on Wednesday that China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all. Addressing the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in the southern metropolis of Shenzhen, Xi called on business communities in the region to uphold the entrepreneurial spirit and make greater contributions to economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. Under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the two-day meeting has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland. "The Asia-Pacific is our home; it is here we jointly pursue development and cooperation," Xi said. Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has been one of the world's most dynamic engines of growth. Today, the APEC economies are home to about 40 percent of the world's population, and account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of global trade. As the world becomes more turbulent and the global economy lacks growth momentum, the Chinese president said the region must answer the "hard questions of our times": to open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways? In his response, Xi put forward proposals on how the region can prosper together, calling on APEC economies to uphold peace and stability, build bridges of opening-up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth and expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. All parties in the region must "uphold the postwar international order," he said, calling on them to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation and address challenges through solidarity and coordination.

item.title: Regional development, connectivity stressed
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Editor's note: President Xi Jinping held six bilateral talks with leaders attending the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Tuesday. President Xi Jinping called on Tuesday for China and Vietnam to enhance mutual trust and solidarity, deepen comprehensive cooperation, and jointly safeguard peace and stability and promote development and prosperity. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during a meeting with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam in Shenzhen. He described China and Vietnam as "comrades and brothers", saying that "the rougher the seas, the more we must pull together". While calling for promoting the alignment of their interests, Xi underlined the need for both countries to boost connectivity, advance the early establishment of smart ports and cross-border economic cooperation zones, expand collaboration in digital transformation and green, low-carbon development, and explore partnership in applications of artificial intelligence. He called on both sides to properly manage their differences in the South China Sea issue, steadily advance maritime cooperation, and strengthen cooperation within frameworks such as the United Nations, China-ASEAN cooperation, and Lancang-Mekong cooperation. Xi also expressed China's willingness to strengthen mutual learning with Vietnam in development experiences, firmly support each other, and deepen exchanges on party self-supervision and self-governance. To Lam expressed his congratulations on the successful convening of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee. He said that Vietnam highly values its relationship with China, and regards it as its most important strategic partner. In the current complex international situation, Vietnam is willing to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with China to aid each other's development, he added. caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi calls for advancing steady, sound development of China-ROK relations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called for advancing the steady and sound development of relations between China and the Republic of Korea (ROK) as next year marks the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two "friendly neighbors and strategic cooperative partners." Xi made the remarks during his meeting with ROK President Lee Jae Myung, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov 18-19. The two countries should uphold strategic independence, maintain the political foundation for bilateral relations, and further consolidate and develop the relationship, Xi stressed. China and the ROK have substantially concluded the second phase of negotiations on the China-ROK Free Trade Agreement. The two countries should make full use of this institutional arrangement to strengthen macroeconomic policy coordination and foster a collaborative ecosystem for emerging technology industries such as artificial intelligence, Xi said. China also stands ready to work with the ROK to facilitate people-to-people exchanges and carry out sound and beneficial cultural exchanges in a step-by-step manner, Xi said. The two sides should further strengthen multilateral coordination, jointly uphold true multilateralism, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community and the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, make greater contributions to regional peace and development, and maintain the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains, Xi said. For his part, Lee said that the two countries have seen sustained momentum in the comprehensive restoration of ROK-China relations, with bilateral economic and trade cooperation growing rapidly, people-to-people exchanges becoming increasingly frequent, and mutual perceptions steadily improving. The ROK's commitment to the one-China principle has not changed and will not change, Lee stressed. The ROK hopes to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, and industrial and supply chains, foster closer people-to-people bonds, and pursue a more mature ROK-China strategic partnership, he said.

item.title: Xi says China-Russia relations bring stability, certainty to turbulent world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping said Wednesday that China-Russia relations have brought greater stability and certainty to a world of turbulence and transformation. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov 18-19. Xi noted that this year marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. He said that China-Russia ties set an example for a new model of major-country relations featuring equality, mutual respect, good faith, and win-win cooperation. Xi called on both countries to deepen all-round cooperation and firmly uphold the due responsibilities and obligations of major countries to guide and promote a multipolar world and democratization of international relations. Both sides should leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between their governments, legislatures, militaries and political parties to ensure that the consensus reached by the two heads of state is effectively implemented, Xi said. Xi called on the two countries to provide a more stable and predictable investment and business environment and protect the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises from both countries. The development of China and Russia is closely intertwined with that of the Asia-Pacific region, and APEC is an important platform for enhancing cooperation, Xi noted. China stands ready to work with the Asia-Pacific family, including Russia, to chart a course for the region's prosperity and development and build an Asia-Pacific community together, Xi said. Putin said he and Xi have held four productive meetings so far this year, helping sustain the sound development momentum in Russia-China relations. High-level exchanges have been close, bilateral trade has reached a new high, and practical cooperation has made substantial progress across various fields, he said. Russia is willing to strengthen back-to-back strategic coordination with China, expand cooperation in trade, energy, education and other fields, and broaden cultural and people-to-people exchanges to better benefit the two peoples, Putin said. Russia also stands ready to work with China to promote development and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, advance the process toward a multipolar world and build a more just and equitable global governance system, he added.

item.title: Xi welcomes Trump at Shenzhen airport
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping on Wednesday welcomed US President Donald Trump at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in South China's Guangdong province. Trump is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov 18-19. Amid welcome music, Xi and Trump shook hands warmly. Honor guards of the Chinese People's Liberation Army presented arms to salute, and a girl handed the US leader a bouquet. The national flags of China and the United States fluttered in the wind as a military band played the national anthems of the two countries, and fighter jets flew overhead in salute. The two heads of state waved to a welcoming young crowd. Xi recalled his state visit to the United States in September this year, when the US presidential couple came to the airport in person and hosted a grand welcoming ceremony, noting that China is a nation with a tradition of courtesy that values reciprocating goodwill.

item.title: Xi hosts welcome banquet for guests attending APEC meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday hosted a banquet in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province, to welcome guests who are here to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. "On behalf of the Chinese government and people, I wish to extend a warm welcome to all the distinguished guests," Xi said in his toast. Openness is deeply rooted in Shenzhen's DNA and innovation drives the city's vitality, while cooperation is where its strength comes from, Xi said, adding that the success of Shenzhen is also a microcosm of China's reform and opening-up, as well as an example of fruitful cooperation across the Asia-Pacific. Noting that openness, innovation and cooperation have been the distinctive features of APEC since its establishment, Xi said APEC has grasped the pulse of the times and guided the process of regional economic integration, making the Asia-Pacific the most dynamic region and a vital growth engine of the world economy. "At the economic leaders' meeting tomorrow, we will discuss measures to expand two-way opening-up, explore paths of innovation-driven growth and unfold more opportunities of practical cooperation in various fields," Xi said.
